capabilities: Synchronize notes and attachments across devices through a GitHub repository
Track deletions, renames and file identities with tombstones and per-device baselines
Resolve conflicting edits with explicit Use LOCAL / Use REMOTE choices instead of automatic merge
Recover interrupted syncs from transaction journals with Resume or Abort actions
Verify remote commits, manifests and local contents before advancing the verified baseline
disambiguation: This is file synchronization, not real-time collaborative editing.
extras: Notes are not end-to-end encrypted; anyone with repository access can read them, so a private repository is advised. Requires Obsidian 1.6.0+, enforces a 20 MiB per-file limit, and the installation ID (local-mirror-sync) differs from the display name for upgrade compatibility.
motivation: The author built it because a git push/pull workflow alone does not handle offline deletions, renames, or interrupted operations, so these questions must be part of the sync protocol itself.
problem: Plain git-style or backup syncing cannot tell whether a missing file was deleted on another device, whether a renamed file is the same file, or whether an interrupted sync actually finished.

relations.evidence: Each device exchanges notes, attachments and file identity information through the same GitHub repository.

requires.name: GitHub account and a private notes repository
GitHub fine-grained personal access token with Contents read/write

summary: Git-based vault synchronization across devices via GitHub with verified baselines, deletion tombstones, rename tracking and explicit conflict review.
